rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill (it has `name:` front matter), so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references`. The requirement obliges each link to a specialized file to say when to read that file.

The file has one Markdown link, `[CI example](../habeas/references/ci.md)`, in workflow step 9. It sits in the instruction to recommend separate collection and `habeas coverage-check` steps in project CI, "using the Habeas CI example". That ties the file to a specific situation, which is when you write that CI recommendation. I read this as meeting the obligation.

The skill also points to `references/authoring-failures.md`, `references/distributed-requirements.md` and `references/fixme.md`. These are inline-code mentions, not links. Each one still says when to read it:
- `authoring-failures.md`: "If it fails, read ...".
- `distributed-requirements.md`: when proposing a distributed requirement for a convention that applies at many sites.
- `fixme.md`: when the user defers a possible bug.

I found no link that lacks a statement of when to read it, and there are no violation matches to judge.
